Naturally, they've seen how agents often miscommunicate and misunderstand one another, and how semantic and cognitive misalignments between agents can quickly compound into major performance degradation. To help others avoid similar issues, they've recently open-sourced a new suite of protocols designed to help agents think and work productively together. This includes projects called Scope – which builds knowledge graphs on top of agent traces and attempts to identify cognitive failures; Accord – which helps agents align on intent, scope, and key terms before work gets underway; and Concord, which helps agents negotiate an outcome every one of them can accept when they disagree. A highlight of this conversation, for me, was the opportunity to compare notes on our personal AI setups. Mine, as regular listeners will know, combines high-access, low-autonomy agents that I think of as "extensions of myself" and that run on my personal laptop, with lower-access, higher-autonomy agents that run on their own computer.
